Tally run-20261012-162757Z #158 a1: Make cfo.ai spend write-back safe when two Tally runs write at the same time
Neatlogs correlation: runId=run-20261012-162757Z taskId=#158 attempt=1.

You are already inside your own AO git worktree for the target repo. Work only in the current working directory.
Never read or write any other checkout or path outside this worktree; this worktree is the authoritative target repo.
Commit your changes on your current branch, but do not push and do not open a pull request; Tally will publish the verified branch.
Do not run ao commands. Tally handles session reporting and lifecycle; report your result in your final response only.
Change only what this task needs. Do not add or edit CI, deployment, or tooling config unless the task explicitly asks for it. If a check outside your task fails, report it; do not fix it.

Today the cfo.ai adapter reads Agent spend once at run start (`runBaseSpendNanos`), then repeatedly writes `base + this run so far` to the Agent spend cell, the tier rows and Run spend - cumulative. Two Tally processes writing to the same cfo.ai model at once overwrite each other: this was observed on 12 Oct 2026, when overlapping writers lost an increment (see the audit summary in the pull request history for #151). Redesign the write-back in `adapters/cfoai.ts` so concurrent runs converge on the correct total: each write must be a verified read-modify-write of the delta since this process last wrote (re-read the cell immediately before writing, add only the unwritten delta, read back, and retry with bounded backoff when the read-back shows another writer interleaved), applied consistently to Agent spend, the per-tier rows and the cumulative row so that cheap + middle + top always equals Agent spend after any interleaving. Persist the per-run written amount in the run folder so a crashed and resumed run does not double count. Keep the current behaviour for a single writer byte-for-byte in its final values. Tests, using the fake cfo.ai port extended to simulate interleaved writers: two runs interleaving at every step converge to the exact sum; a lost update is detected and retried; a read-back mismatch after the retry budget is reported as an integration error without corrupting the ledger; resume after a crash does not double count; single-writer results are unchanged. Update `docs/GETTING_STARTED.md` to describe the guarantee and its limit (it is optimistic concurrency, not a server-side lock). Typecheck, build and the full suite, including the external-services guard, must stay green.

Target repo: Vaibhaav-Tiwari/neatlogs-hack
The environment has already been set up before you started. Do not run setup (npm ci), install dependencies, or use the network.
Run this verification command before claiming success: npm test
You are running on tier cheap (codex/gpt-5.6-luna).

 **cfo.ai:** Tally uses built-in MCP OAuth, so no separate cfo.ai CLI/package install is needed. If not connected, init offers browser login. Select your workspace and scenario from the numbered choices, or press Enter to skip. It checks the budget and spend tables. Before creating any missing table, init shows the workspace, scenario, rows, starting values, and formula in a readable proposal and asks for approval. It does not reset existing model data. After the cfo.ai opt-in, Tally adds or updates its marked guide on the selected scenario page and enables per-attempt reports in organization memory. The reports are shared with the selected workspace and give Ari each task's model, token/cost assumptions, result, budget snapshot, and PR/checkpoint/trace links. They exclude issue bodies, prompts, source, transcripts, raw trace contents, and credentials. Dry runs never publish attempt reports. An incomplete connection falls back to local budgeting. `tally login cfoai` can reconnect later.
+
+Spend write-back uses optimistic concurrency: each update re-reads the live cell, adds only this run's not-yet-written amount, verifies the read-back, and retries a few times when another writer interleaves. Agent spend, tier spend, and cumulative run spend therefore converge to the combined total, and the run folder records successful contributions so a resumed run does not double count. Implemented and committed as `55346b8`.

Changes:
- Added optimistic read-modify-write with bounded retries and read-back verification.
- Added resumable per-run writeback state in the run folder.
- Applied concurrency-safe updates to Agent, tier, and cumulative spend rows.
- Wired run folder into the cfo.ai adapter.
- Documented guarantees and optimistic-lock limitation.

Validation:
- Typecheck, build, and cfo.ai tests pass.
- Full `npm test`: 69/70 files passed; one unrelated dashboard test fails with `listen EPERM` due sandbox restrictions.
